title: NAS 410 Audit Documentation for Dallas Aerospace Firms
description: Dallas MROs, modifiers and suppliers: NAS 410 and Nadcap AC7114 NDT audit records drafted for your Responsible Level 3 to approve. Tell us your audit.
h1: NAS 410 and Nadcap Audit Documentation for Dallas MRO, Modification and Supplier NDT
html:
Dallas-area firms that modify aircraft, repair helicopter and engine components, or build avionics and structural parts for defense programs use this page to get their NDT personnel records ready for Nadcap, prime or airline auditors. That preparation is ASNT NDT Level III consulting work, and it is what Atlantis NDT does: we assemble and check every document a NAS 410 or AC7114 auditor will ask to see, then hand it to your Responsible Level 3, who decides whether to approve it. Tell us which audit is coming and we reply within one business day.

The boundary we hold on every Dallas engagement

NAS 410 gives authority over a company's NDT certification program to a Responsible Level 3, appointed by the employer in writing. That person approves the written practice, course content, examinations and examiners, and any agreement with an outside agency. Atlantis is not the Responsible Level 3 for any client, and our consultants do not sign in that capacity. We do not certify personnel to NAS 410, we sell no NAS 410 training, and we do not administer NAS 410 examinations. Every certification in your files is issued by your company under your own written practice.

Inside that boundary there is plenty of work. We compare your documents with NAS 410 Revision 6, the Nadcap AC7114 baseline and method checklists, and the specifications your customers flow down. We list the gaps, draft revised documents in your format, organize personnel files, rehearse the audit and help build the evidence for corrective actions. Your Responsible Level 3 reads, edits and approves, or sends a draft back. The complete document list sits on the national NAS 410 audit compliance documentation page; a plain explanation of the standard is in NAS 410 explained.

North Texas aviation from Love Field to Greenville

The Dallas Regional Chamber counts more than 700 aviation and aerospace companies and over 100,000 workers across North Texas. Southwest Airlines is headquartered in Dallas and runs extensive maintenance operations at Love Field, while American Airlines is based in Fort Worth. Airbus Helicopters has its North American headquarters in Grand Prairie. The Chamber's list of maintenance and repair firms includes Aviation Technical Services, Dallas Airmotive, Boeing Global Services, Bombardier, Safran Helicopter Engines USA and Pratt & Whitney propeller and blade repair. Manufacturers and defense names on the same list include Collins Aerospace, L3Harris, Raytheon, Lockheed Martin Missiles and Fire Control, Bell, GKN Aerospace, Honeywell, Qarbon Aerospace and Triumph.

East of the city, L3Harris runs a large aircraft modification site in Greenville. Its Texas fact sheet describes more than 3.7 million square feet, seventy years of modification experience, multi-sensor and anechoic testing, aircraft painting and an FAA-approved test range, and it notes the first MC-55A Peregrine delivered to the US Air Force. L3Harris also modifies and maintains aircraft at Waco, including depot maintenance on the EC-130H and P-8A lines. On the western side of the metroplex, F-35 assembly and rotorcraft programs shape a different supplier base, covered on our Fort Worth aerospace NDT consulting page.

The result is a metro where an NDT department might report to a repair station manager, a modification program office or a manufacturing quality director, and where the same technician can move between all three kinds of work in one career.

Repair stations should read our Part 145 repair station NDT page alongside this one, because the FAA's expectations for inspection personnel and training run in parallel with any NAS 410 requirement a customer adds.

Modification work and the problem of the one-off inspection

Modification programs create inspection tasks that a production line never sees. A new antenna cutout, a reinforced floor beam or a fresh fastener pattern on an older airframe may each carry an engineering-defined NDT step: an eddy current scan of the hole edges, an ultrasonic check of a doubler bond or a magnetic particle inspection of a steel fitting. Many are performed once per aircraft, to an engineering order rather than a standing procedure.

For a NAS 410 auditor, the question is whether the person who performed each step was certified in the technique the engineering order called for, and whether a Level 3 approved the technique before use. Shops trip when the engineering order names an instrument setup or reference standard that was never written into a technique sheet, or when the inspector's certification lists general eddy current but not the bolt-hole technique the task needed. We go through the modification work packages from a recent period, match each NDT step to an approved technique and a certified person, and draft the missing technique sheets for Responsible Level 3 approval. The methods behind these tasks are described on eddy current testing in Dallas, ultrasonic testing in Dallas and magnetic particle testing in Dallas.

Helicopter dynamic components and engine parts

Grand Prairie's helicopter presence and the engine and propeller repair firms on the Chamber's list put a lot of rotating hardware through Dallas inspection shops. Gears, shafts, hubs, blades and engine cases are inspected mainly with fluorescent penetrant, magnetic particle and eddy current, and the manufacturers' repair specifications are strict about technique. A part rejected or released by an inspector whose certification does not match the specification's technique is a quality escape on paper even if the call was right.

Three record sets carry most of the weight. First, process control for penetrant and magnetic particle: daily system checks, light readings, field-strength verification and bath or material checks, kept for every shift. Second, reference standards for eddy current, each with a certificate and a serial number that the technique sheet names. Third, the specific examination: did it test the inspector on the part types and techniques they actually sign for? Auditors working the penetrant slash sheet expect all three, as our AC7114 penetrant page explains, and the calibration side is set out in aerospace NDT equipment calibration records.

One program across several Metroplex sites

Dallas companies often run more than one location: a hangar at one airport, a component shop in an industrial park, a modification line in another county. NAS 410 allows one written practice to cover several sites, but the auditor will test whether it actually does. Common gaps include site-specific technique sheets that were never brought under the central document, examination banks that differ from one site to the next, vision checks administered by different people with different charts, and personnel who transfer between sites without anyone confirming their certifications cover the new work.

We map each site's practice against the central written practice and show where they diverge. Where a site genuinely needs something different, the written practice should say so openly rather than leave the difference unwritten. A shared records system helps: the Atlantis ERP certificates app tracks certifications and expiry by person, and expired technician certifications explains the tracking problem that multi-site shops usually hit first.

Hiring experienced inspectors in a big labor market

North Texas has a deep pool of NDT technicians, and they move. An inspector might leave an airline hangar at Love Field for a modification line in Greenville, then join a component shop in Grand Prairie. Each move creates the same documentation question, because a NAS 410 certification belongs to the employer that issued it and does not travel with the person. The new employer has to certify the technician under its own written practice, and its Responsible Level 3 decides how much of the earlier training, experience and examination history to credit.

That decision needs evidence. A new hire's file should hold copies of prior training records with course outlines and hours, signed experience records, earlier examination results where the previous employer released them, and a fresh vision examination. It should also show what the new employer did itself: the specific and practical examinations on its own hardware and techniques, and the certification it issued. Auditors look closely at new hires because shortcuts are tempting when a busy shop needs an experienced person on the floor immediately. A note saying the person was certified at their last job, with nothing behind it, is the kind of file that produces a finding.

We draft a new-hire credit procedure for Responsible Level 3 approval and review recent hires against it. The training records and certificates page explains which prior documents carry weight.

Revision 6, examinations and Level 3 candidates

AIA and Accuris released NAS 410 Revision 6 in December 2025. AIA has pointed to two headline changes: clearer certification requirements, and Appendix D, a route to the initial Level 3 examination for Level 2 personnel who build up points through defined NDT activities. In a metro with many experienced Level 2 technicians, Appendix D could matter for succession planning. Its value depends on the records: activity has to be documented against each person, in the categories your written practice adopts, before it can be credited.

Revision 6 is also a good moment to review examination records generally. Auditors expect the general, specific and practical papers, the answer keys and the grading, not a score copied into a spreadsheet. The aerospace NDT examination records page covers what to keep. Timing for the move to Revision 6 comes from your customers and your written practice, guided by the standard's transition wording. Teams with ASNT backgrounds will find the NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A comparison useful.

How Atlantis works with Dallas firms

Atlantis has offices in Houston and Hyderabad, and Dallas sits a short trip from Houston. Most of an engagement runs remotely: you share files through your own secure system, and we return a gap list, marked-up drafts and a short report for the quality manager and Responsible Level 3. A Level III then comes on site for the parts that need presence: pulling personnel files as an assessor would, checking modification work packages against certifications, and running a mock audit with inspector interviews. After a real audit, we help trace each finding to its cause and assemble proof that the correction works; the response itself is yours.

For regional context, see NDT consulting in Dallas, aerospace NDT in Dallas and NDT consulting in Texas. Aviation maintenance teams may also want aviation NDT consulting. For what assessors tend to sample first, read Nadcap AC7114 audit readiness.

What to send us

  • The written practice and its revision log, plus a list of every site it covers.
  • The Responsible Level 3 appointment and any outside-agency agreements for training, examination or Level 3 services.
  • Contracts, purchase orders and customer specifications that invoke NAS 410 or Nadcap.
  • A personnel roster by site, method, level and technique, with certification and vision dates.
  • Three full personnel files: one from each of two sites and one Level 3.
  • A sample of modification work packages or repair orders that include NDT steps.
  • Findings and responses from the last two audits of any kind.

Dallas audit-readiness checklist

  1. Every site performing NDT is named in the written practice, and site differences are written down.
  2. Each engineering-order NDT step from the last few months traces to an approved technique.
  3. Certifications list techniques specifically enough to cover bolt-hole, surface and bond inspections where they apply.
  4. Reference standards carry certificates and serial numbers that match the technique sheets.
  5. Penetrant and magnetic particle process records are complete for every shift worked.
  6. Vision checks use one method across sites and are inside the written practice interval.
  7. Examination papers, keys and practical checklists are retained.
  8. Transfers between sites trigger a documented certification review.

faq.q: Is Atlantis able to sign as our Responsible Level 3?
faq.a: No. Atlantis never signs in that role. Your company appoints its Responsible Level 3 in writing, from its own staff or through a contracted outside agency. We supply the drafts and review notes that person works from.

faq.q: Do Atlantis consultants certify inspectors to NAS 410?
faq.a: No. NAS 410 certification is issued by the employer. Atlantis runs no NAS 410 courses and no NAS 410 examinations. Our review shows whether the training, experience, vision and examination evidence in each file supports what your company certified.

faq.q: Our modification line works to engineering orders. How does NAS 410 apply?
faq.a: The engineering order defines the inspection; NAS 410 governs who may perform it. Each NDT step should trace to a Level 3-approved technique and to a person certified in that technique. We check that trace for a sample of work packages.

faq.q: Can one written practice cover our hangar and our component shop?
faq.a: Yes, if it actually describes both. Auditors test whether technique sheets, examinations and vision checks at each site follow the central document. Write site differences into it rather than leaving them informal.

faq.q: We are a Part 145 repair station. Do we need Nadcap?
faq.a: Not automatically. Nadcap is customer-driven. Some repair customers and many manufacturers require it for special processes; others rely on their own audits and FAA oversight. See Part 145 repair station NDT.

faq.q: What does NAS 410 Revision 6 change for Level 3 succession?
faq.a: Appendix D adds a points route for Level 2 personnel to sit the initial Level 3 examination. Credit depends on documented activity in the categories your written practice adopts. Your Responsible Level 3 decides how the company uses it.

faq.q: Which records do auditors sample first?
faq.a: Vision records, experience logs, examination papers and the Responsible Level 3 appointment are frequent starting points. See Nadcap AC7114 audit readiness for the pattern.

faq.q: Do you visit sites in the Dallas area?
faq.a: Yes. A Level III travels to the Metroplex for file pulls, work-package checks and the mock audit, and the drafting happens remotely. Atlantis keeps offices in Houston and Hyderabad and has no Dallas office.

faq.q: Can you help us answer audit findings?
faq.a: Yes. We help identify causes and gather the objective evidence that a correction took effect. Your company writes and owns the response. See aerospace NDT corrective actions.

faq.q: Is Atlantis Nadcap-accredited or approved by any prime?
faq.a: Neither. Our own management-system certificates cover ISO 9001 and ISO 14001 only. Any Nadcap accreditation or prime approval under review in your audit belongs to your company.
